newsitem.title: FRANCE: SocGen renews attack on Credit Lyonnais bailout.
newsitem.headline: SocGen renews attack on Credit Lyonnais bailout.

text.p: French bank Societe Generale, renewing its attack on state aid to Credit Lyonnais, said on Monday it wanted the government to consider breaking up its rival and selling off most of its operations.

Societe Generale head Marc Vienot wrote to European Commissioner Karel Van Miert last month asking him to make the French government review "alternative solutions for the controlled liquidation and sale of blocks" of Credit Lyonnais, a bank spokesman said.

The Commission must clear all state aid to the bank, still suffering from a heady expansion spree in the late 1980s which backfired and led to massive losses. The government is hoping to privatise the bank as soon as possible.
Afternoon daily Le Monde said the British had also expressed concerns to the Commission about French state aid to the bank.

The Societe Generale spokesman said Vienot asked "for the sale of all its (Credit Lyonnais') overseas activities...as well as its domestic operations such as investment management, consumer credit and perhaps a fraction of its retail network".
"But it's up to the shareholder (the state) to decide," the spokesman said.
The bank has sold many of its South American activities but has been resistant to selling its U.S., Asian or European operations.

Meanwhile, Le Monde reported the Commission believed state aid to the bank to ready it for privatisation could total 30 billion francs ($5.3 billion). The government and Credit Lyonnais still are negotiating the privatisation plan.

The aid would be on top of 45 billion francs in support from the French taxpayer the bank received in 1995 and 3.9 billion francs in emergency help it got in 1996 to allow it to report a modest profit.
Societe Generale said it would challenge the 3.9 billion franc handout in the European Court of Justice in Luxembourg before mid-March.
It filed a similar challenge in the European court last year against the 1995 state rescue of Credit Lyonnais.

"We're tenacious," the bank spokesman said, referring to Societe Generale's unrelenting campaign against aid to Credit Lyonnais which it says represents preferential treatment to the state bank during a difficult period for the entire sector.

The Societe Generale spokesman also objected to Credit Lyonnais' claims that it needed to boost its Cooke ratio -- an international banking solvency standard -- to six percent from its current 4.5 percent to be privatised.
"We were privatised in 1987 with (a Cooke ratio) of three percent. We have climbed up to six percent but we did it by ourselves," said the spokesman.
